role: Ananya (Frontend) — SPA production-readiness audit, RC commit 115f698 (clean checkout at C:/Users/Sage world/AppData/Local/Temp/claude/rc-115f698)
summary: Audited the Vite + React 18 + react-router-dom SPA (src/App.tsx, src/pages, src/components, src/admin, src/lib) at commit 115f698, checked out clean and audited only from that directory. `tsc --noEmit` passes clean (E4, exit 0) and CI runs it as a separate gate — but `npm run build` is literally `vite build` with no typecheck plugin in vite.config.ts, so the production build itself does not typecheck (this is documented as a known-fixed CI gap, but the build script itself is still typecheck-blind). A full production build was run in this session with the repo's own .env.production (VITE_API_MODE=live, real API base URL) and completed in ~15.5 min, producing a single 3.37 MB (899 KB gzip) main JS chunk — none of the ~100 page components in App.tsx use React.lazy/route-level code-splitting, so every visitor, including an anonymous landing-page visit, downloads virtually the whole brand+creator+admin+3D bundle up front. Auth architecture is asymmetric across the three realms: brand/creator sessions (F-0551) hold the access token in memory only with an HttpOnly refresh cookie and a hardened 401→refresh→retry→hard-redirect-to-login path (F-0438); the admin realm stores its access token in localStorage (mitigated by a short 900s expiry + rotation) but its own 401→refresh→retry handler in src/admin/services/api-contracts.ts only clears the token on definitive failure — it never calls the admin equivalent of `redirectToLogin`, so a mid-session admin whose token/refresh is revoked is left rendering the console with failing calls until they manually navigate, instead of being bounced to /admin/login the way brand/creator explicitly were fixed to be. The Razorpay checkout wrapper (src/lib/razorpay.ts) is correctly designed as UI-only — it never trusts the Checkout `handler` callback as proof of payment and documents that callers must re-verify server-side — and the client-side money-flag gate that blocks withdraw/fund/top-up when payments are disabled is covered by a passing runtime test (9/9, E4) that asserts `fetch` is never called. Two built, wired-together pieces of the Meera AI credit-metering feature (`useMeeraCredits` hook and `CreditMeter` component, both P13-labelled) are completely orphaned — zero references anywhere else in src/, including no CREDITS_EXHAUSTED/402 handling in the real brand-chat.tsx — so real users get no visible credit meter or paywall UI for Meera today. Two more real, non-trivial components are similarly dead code: `CounterProposalCard` (creator deal-room accept/decline card) and `HeroGlobe` (3D hero). No without alt was found, and the main site nav has correct aria-labels for its icon-only hamburger button. A full vitest run and a full manual pass over all ~100 pages' loading/empty/error states was out of scope for the time available; this report is based on direct source reading, config/CI inspection, a real `tsc --noEmit` run, a real production `vite build`, and one targeted vitest run of the money-flag gate suite.

questions.question: Does `npm run build` (the actual production build command) type-check the codebase, or only `npm run typecheck`?
questions.why_it_matters: If the build script itself doesn't typecheck, a type error can ship in any pipeline that runs `build` without also running `typecheck` as a separate, non-skippable step.
questions.answer: No. `package.json`'s `build` script is `vite build` (Rollup/esbuild transform only); `vite.config.ts` has no `vite-plugin-checker` or any TS-checking plugin. `typecheck` (`tsc -p tsconfig.json --noEmit`) is a separate script. CI (`.github/workflows/frontend-checks.yml`) does run both as separate steps in the same job, with a comment stating this was a known-fixed gap ("vite build alone does NOT typecheck"), so in THIS repo's CI a type error is caught — but only because both steps are wired into the same required job, not because `build` itself checks types.
questions.evidence: package.json scripts block (`"build": "vite build"`, separate `"typecheck": "tsc -p tsconfig.json --noEmit"`); vite.config.ts has no checker plugin (grep for checker/typescript/tsc returned nothing); .github/workflows/frontend-checks.yml lines 39-95 run `npm run typecheck` and `npm run build` as separate steps in job `typecheck · test · build`.
questions.remaining_uncertainty: Did not check every deploy path (e.g. a Docker build stage) to confirm it always runs both steps rather than `build` alone.

questions.question: Is the SPA route tree code-split, so a first-time visitor to the public landing page isn't forced to download the brand/creator/admin dashboards too?
questions.why_it_matters: A monolithic bundle directly hurts LCP/TTI for the highest-traffic, least-authenticated pages (landing, pricing, public portfolio) which are also the pages most exposed to organic/paid traffic and mobile networks.
questions.answer: No. Every one of the ~100 page components imported in src/App.tsx (BrandLoginPage, BrandDashboardPage, AdminConsolePage, CreatorChatPage, etc.) is a static top-level `import ... from '@/pages/...'`, not `React.lazy(() => import(...))`. Only two isolated pieces (a 3D login scene on a dev-only page, and MeeraDemoPlayer on the marketing meera-for-creators page) use dynamic `import()`. This matches the single 899 KB-gzip main chunk observed in the real build output.

questions.question: Are the brand/creator and admin auth realms consistent in how they store tokens and recover from a session dying mid-use?
questions.why_it_matters: The admin console explicitly handles money/KYC/moderation (per its own route-guard comment) — an inconsistency here is higher-stakes than the same inconsistency on a marketing page.
questions.answer: No, they diverge in two ways. (1) Storage: brand/creator access tokens live in memory only (src/lib/api.ts HttpClient.getToken/setToken, per the F-0551 hardening comment) with the refresh token in an HttpOnly cookie; the admin access token is stored in localStorage (src/admin/services/admin-session.ts ADMIN_TOKEN_KEY='admin_token') — mitigated by a short 900s expiry + server-side rotation on every refresh, but still a JS-readable token at rest, unlike brand/creator's memory-only design. (2) Failure handling: brand/creator's `fetchWithAuthRetry` (src/lib/api.ts ~line 647-658) explicitly calls `redirectToLogin(role)` (a hard `window.location.href` navigation) when a 401's follow-up refresh also fails, with a comment (F-0438) stating this was fixed specifically because leaving the user on a dead page until their next navigation was a known bug. The admin equivalent, `apiRequest` in src/admin/services/api-contracts.ts (lines 130-143), on the same refresh-fails-too path only calls `clearAdminToken()` — no navigate/redirect call anywhere in that function or file. Grepping the whole src/admin tree for a reactive redirect-on-auth-failure found only the manual Logout button's `navigate('/admin/login')` in AdminLayout.tsx, which fires on an explicit click, not on session death.
questions.evidence: src/lib/use-auth-guard-state.ts (memory+cookie based check); src/lib/api.ts lines 468-500 (getToken/setToken split by isApiLive) and lines 647-658 (401→refresh→retry→redirectToLogin, F-0438 comment); src/admin/services/admin-session.ts lines 38-112 (localStorage-based ADMIN_TOKEN_KEY, getAdminToken/setAdminToken/clearAdminToken); src/admin/services/api-contracts.ts lines 106-164 (apiRequest, no redirect on refresh failure); src/admin/components/AdminLayout.tsx line 108-116 (only a manual-logout navigate).
questions.remaining_uncertainty: Did not runtime-reproduce an actual admin-session-death scenario (would require a live/staging admin JWT to expire or be revoked mid-session); this is a direct code-level comparison, not an observed runtime failure. It's also possible some outer admin route wrapper (not found in this pass) polls or listens for token clearance and redirects — none was found in src/admin, src/App.tsx, or src/pages/admin-console.tsx's top-level wiring, but the admin tree is large.

questions.question: Is the Razorpay checkout integration safe against a client claiming payment succeeded when it did not?
questions.why_it_matters: Trusting a client-side payment callback as proof of a fund transfer is a classic money-safety bug (fabricated success, race conditions, tampered response).
questions.answer: The wrapper itself is built correctly: src/lib/razorpay.ts's `openRazorpayCheckout` never marks anything as paid — its own header comment states "[Checkout's] `handler` callback is untrusted... callers MUST verify funding via a server-confirmed status" and the function only forwards the SDK's response to the caller's `onSuccess`, doing no state mutation itself. The publishable key is always fetched from `GET /config/razorpay`, never hardcoded, and the module documents it never accepts a secret.
questions.evidence: src/lib/razorpay.ts lines 1-18 (header comment on money-safety posture) and 152-189 (openRazorpayCheckout implementation — handler just calls the passed-in onSuccess, no local balance/state mutation).
questions.remaining_uncertainty: This audit did not open every CALLER of openRazorpayCheckout (e.g. FundEscrowButton.tsx, brand-wallet.tsx's topUp flow) to confirm each one actually re-verifies against the server before updating UI state, rather than trusting onSuccess directly — the wrapper's contract is sound but caller compliance was not individually re-verified in this pass beyond what the wrapper's own comments describe (useEscrowFund.ts / brand-wallet.tsx polling GET /wallet/escrow/{id} and GET /wallet).

questions.question: Does a render crash on one page take down the whole SPA, and is crash reporting safe (never throws, never blocks the fallback)?
questions.why_it_matters: This is the single most important resilience property for an SPA with ~100 routes — one bad page must not white-screen the whole session.
questions.answer: The error boundary is correctly scoped: `RoutedErrorBoundary` in App.tsx wraps `<Routes>` INSIDE `<BrowserRouter>` and resets its `hasError` state via a `resetKey` tied to `location.pathname`, with an explicit comment (CR-10) describing the prior bug (mounted outside the Router, so one crash killed routing for the rest of the session) and how this fixes it. The crash-reporting side-effect (`reportCrash` in ErrorBoundary.tsx) is wrapped in nested try/catch, is fire-and-forget (never awaited), and dedupes per session on a JSON-encoded `[message, pathname]` key so a render loop can't flood the report endpoint.
questions.evidence: src/App.tsx lines 187-201 (RoutedErrorBoundary + CR-10 comment) and 210 (mounted inside BrowserRouter, wrapping <Routes>); src/components/ErrorBoundary.tsx lines 62-125 (componentDidCatch → reportCrash, try/catch nesting, reportedCrashKeys Set dedupe, componentDidUpdate resetting hasError only on resetKey change).
questions.remaining_uncertainty: Did not runtime-trigger an actual render crash in a browser to observe the fallback UI and confirm the POST to /api/v1/client-errors fires as described; this is direct code-reading only (E2/E3, not E4 for this specific behavior).

questions.question: Do the brand/creator registration forms validate consistently and map server error codes back to the correct field, rather than showing a generic toast?
questions.why_it_matters: Generic error toasts on a field-specific server rejection (e.g. "phone already exists") force users to guess which field is wrong, directly hurting signup conversion.
questions.answer: Yes, on the one form inspected in depth. `creator-register.tsx`'s `validate()` does real client-side checks (name, email regex, phone via `normalizePhone`/`isValidPhone`, password length ≥8, confirm-password match, terms acceptance) before submit, and `submitRegistration`'s catch block branches on the server's machine-readable `err.code` (e.g. `PHONE_ALREADY_EXISTS`) rather than the bare HTTP status, explicitly because the same endpoint also 409s for `EMAIL_ALREADY_EXISTS` and status-only branching would mislabel one as the other.
questions.evidence: src/pages/creator-register.tsx lines 78-108 (validate function) and lines 159-169 (catch block branching on `err.code === 'PHONE_ALREADY_EXISTS'`, with a comment explaining why status-alone branching would be wrong).

findings.title: Admin session does not force a re-login when it dies mid-use — only clears localStorage, unlike the fixed brand/creator path
findings.evidence: src/admin/services/api-contracts.ts apiRequest() (lines 130-143): on a 401 whose follow-up refresh also fails, it calls `clearAdminToken()` and nothing else — no navigate/redirect anywhere in that function or file. Contrast with src/lib/api.ts fetchWithAuthRetry() (lines 647-658), which on the identical failure mode calls `this.clearToken(role); redirectToLogin(role);` — a hard `window.location.href` navigation — with an explicit F-0438 comment stating this was fixed BECAUSE 'leaving them on a dead page until their next navigation happens to re-run the route guard' was a real bug for brand/creator. Grepped all of src/admin for any other redirect-on-auth-failure path; the only `navigate('/admin/login')` found is the manual Logout button handler in src/admin/components/AdminLayout.tsx (fires on click, not on session death).
findings.location: src/admin/services/api-contracts.ts:130-143 (apiRequest); compare src/lib/api.ts:647-658 (fetchWithAuthRetry, F-0438 fix) and src/admin/components/AdminLayout.tsx:108-116 (manual logout only)
findings.impact: An admin whose token is revoked, whose account is deactivated, or whose 30-day refresh cookie expires while they have the console open in an idle tab is not redirected to /admin/login. They are left staring at a rendered but functionally dead console — the visible data goes stale and every subsequent action shows the generic 'Request failed' fallback message the same file already documents (line ~146-154) as poor UX — until they manually reload or navigate away. Because the admin console is explicitly the money/KYC/moderation surface (per the route guard's own header comment), a support agent debugging 'the admin panel is broken' for this operator would not immediately suspect an expired session, since nothing tells them to log back in.
findings.recommended_fix: In api-contracts.ts's apiRequest(), on the refresh-fails branch, call the same kind of hard redirect brand/creator already uses (e.g. a small admin-specific `redirectToAdminLogin()` mirroring src/lib/api.ts's `redirectToLogin`), guarded the same way (skip if already on /admin/login) so a route already there doesn't loop.
findings.verification_required: Reproduce by minting a short-lived admin JWT + refresh cookie in a controlled/staging admin account, letting both expire while the console is open, then triggering any apiRequest call and observing whether the browser navigates to /admin/login or stays on the dead page.

Output: `dist/assets/index-VeUi4oUB.js  3,373.53 kB │ gzip: 899.29 kB` plus a second `PerformanceMonitor-*.js 894.33 kB │ gzip: 241.84 kB` chunk, both flagged by Vite's own '(!) Some chunks are larger than 500 kB' warning. src/App.tsx imports every one of its ~100 page components (BrandDashboardPage, AdminConsolePage, CreatorChatPage, LandingPage, etc.) via static top-level `import`, not `React.lazy`; only two isolated leaf components elsewhere use dynamic import(). vite.config.ts has no manualChunks/rollupOptions.output configuration.
findings.location: src/App.tsx:11-91 (static page imports), :203-895 (Routes with no Suspense/lazy boundaries); vite.config.ts (no chunking config); build artifact dist/assets/index-VeUi4oUB.js

findings.title: Meera AI credit-metering feature (usage meter + paywall) is fully built but never rendered or wired into the live Meera chat page

findings.title: Admin access token stored in localStorage, not memory-only — architecturally weaker than the brand/creator (F-0551) design in the same codebase
findings.evidence: src/admin/services/admin-session.ts: `export const ADMIN_TOKEN_KEY = 'admin_token'` and `setAdminToken`/`getAdminToken` read/write `localStorage` directly. Contrast with src/lib/api.ts's HttpClient, whose F-0551 comment (line 20-41) explicitly moved brand/creator access tokens to memory-only specifically to close an 'XSS-exfiltration surface.' The admin module's own header comment acknowledges the token stays short-lived (900s) with server-side rotation as the mitigation.
findings.location: src/admin/services/admin-session.ts:38-112 (localStorage-based token storage); compare src/lib/api.ts:442-500 (memory-only token storage, F-0551)
findings.impact: Any XSS in the admin console (a lower-traffic, more privileged surface) has a slightly larger window to read a live admin bearer token directly out of localStorage than the equivalent brand/creator token, which never touches persistent storage. The 900s expiry + rotation meaningfully bounds the blast radius, which is why this is P3 rather than higher, but the inconsistency itself is worth a deliberate call rather than an accidental one.
findings.recommended_fix: Consider migrating the admin access token to the same memory-only pattern as brand/creator, now that admin-session.ts already has the refresh-cookie infrastructure in place to support it.
findings.verification_required: None beyond the code read already done here; this is a design-consistency observation, not a reproducible bug.
